```{r policy-table}
w_sub <- my$term_subaru

policies <- tibble(
  Policy = c(
    "Franchised dealer throughout",
    "Toyota stays to hold the cover; Subaru leaves when free",
    "Both leave when free — the extra cover declined"
  ),
  cost = c(
    cost_of(my$rate, dealer_anyway = TRUE)$pv_dkk,
    cost_of(my$rate, dealer_anyway = FALSE)$pv_dkk,
    # Both tied to their own dealer to the same point, both independent after:
    # what remains is the brand penalty alone.
    cost_of(my$rate, dealer_anyway = TRUE, horizon = w_sub)$pv_dkk
  ),
  gap_a = c(my$gap_full[["A"]], my$gap_full[["A"]], 0),
  gap_b = c(my$gap_full[["B"]], my$gap_full[["B"]], 0)
) |>
  mutate(net_a = gap_a - cost, net_b = gap_b - cost)

policies |>
  transmute(
    `Servicing policy` = Policy,
    `Cost of choosing Toyota` = paste0(fmt_dkk(cost), " DKK"),
    `Cover gained` = ifelse(gap_b <= 0, "none",
                            paste0(fmt_dkk(gap_a), "–", fmt_dkk(gap_b), " DKK")),
    `Net, calibration A` = paste0(fmt_dkk(net_a), " DKK"),
    `Net, calibration B` = paste0(fmt_dkk(net_b), " DKK")
  ) |>
  show_table(caption = paste0(
    "At ", fmt_km(my$rate), " km/yr. Subaru's guarantee lapses in year ",
    fmt_num(w_sub), ", which is when a Subaru owner becomes free to leave."
  ))
```

**The sign does not depend on the servicing policy.** Toyota is behind under all three, and by a similar margin under the two coherent extremes — `r fmt_dkk(-policies$net_b[1])` DKK if you dealer-service throughout, `r fmt_dkk(-policies$net_b[3])` DKK if you both walk away as soon as you are free. The middle row is worse still, but it is the least natural of the three: it has you paying Toyota prices for `r params$age_ceiling` years specifically to hold a guarantee, while a Subaru owner in the same frame of mind has already left.

That is the useful conclusion, because it means **the dealer-versus-independent question does not have to be settled first.** Whichever way you answer it, you would answer it the same way for either car; and on these tariffs the brand penalty runs against Toyota in every case. The one thing that would change the ranking is not your servicing habits but Subaru's prices past `r fmt_km(quoted_to)` km, which nobody has quoted.

What the third row also shows is that **declining the cover is not the cheap escape it looks like.** Walking away at year `r fmt_num(w_sub)` avoids the extra tied visits, but you still paid the brand penalty on the `r sum(vis$km <= w_sub * my$rate)` visits before it — `r fmt_dkk(policies$cost[3])` DKK — and you gave up the ceiling entirely. Buying the Toyota and then declining its distinguishing feature is the worst of the three on calibration B.

### 7.5 Break-even: what would an independent have to charge?

Section 7.4 settled the choice between the cars without needing to know what an independent charges. This section takes up the separate question of whether to *use* one — which you would answer the same way whichever car you bought, but which is worth answering.

Both franchised tariffs are quoted, so the one price still missing is the independent's. Rather than guess it, invert the question: **how cheap would an independent have to be before giving up the Toyota cover is worth it?** That is the only reason to abandon the cover, and it converts the missing number into a threshold a single quote can test.

Raising the independent price raises what a freed Subaru owner pays, shrinking the differential. So for each usage rate there is a single independent price above which the ceiling pays for itself. Quotes *above* the curve mean keep the Toyota cover; quotes *below* it mean the saving beats the cover.

```{r fig-breakeven, fig.height=5}
be_rates <- seq(gap_opens_at * 1.02, max(buyer_rates) * 1.17, length.out = 100)

be <- expand_grid(calib = names(cal), r = be_rates) |>
  mutate(
    gap = map2_dbl(calib, r, \(k, rr) gap_of(cal[[k]], rr)$pv_dkk),
    be = map2_dbl(gap, r, \(g, rr) breakeven_independent(
      g, rr, params$age_ceiling, params$subaru_ceiling_km,
      params$increment_km, price_set(), params$discount_real,
      dealer_anyway = FALSE))
  )

y_top <- max(c(be$be, params$service_margin_high)) * 1.12

ggplot(be, aes(r, be, colour = calib)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = params$service_toyota_small_dkk, colour = pal[["subaru"]],
             linetype = "42", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  annotate("text", x = min(be_rates), y = params$service_toyota_small_dkk,
           label = paste0(" Toyota small service: ",
                          fmt_dkk(params$service_toyota_small_dkk), " DKK/visit"),
           hjust = 0, vjust = -0.6, size = 3, colour = pal[["subaru"]]) +
  geom_text(
    data = be |> group_by(calib) |> slice_max(r, n = 1) |> ungroup(),
    aes(label = paste0("calibration ", calib)),
    hjust = 1, vjust = -0.8, size = 3, show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(c(pal[["A"]], pal[["B"]]), names(cal)),
                      guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = lab_km) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_comma()) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, y_top)) +
  labs(
    title = "What an independent workshop would have to charge",
    subtitle = "An independent quote ABOVE the curve means keeping Toyota cover wins; below it, the saving wins",
    x = "Usage rate (km/yr)", y = "Break-even independent price, small service (DKK)",
    caption = paste0(
      "Dashed line: Toyota's own small-service price of ",
      fmt_dkk(params$service_toyota_small_dkk), " DKK. The break-even curves sit only a little below it, so an\n",
      "independent would have to be barely cheaper than the franchised dealer before the ceiling stopped paying.\n",
      "The sawtooth is real, not noise: visits fall due at fixed odometer points, so a small change in usage can\n",
      "move a whole service in or out of the window and shift the cost by one visit."
    )
  ) +
  theme_note()
```

```{r be-table}
be_tbl <- tibble(rate = buyer_rates[buyer_rates > gap_opens_at]) |>
  mutate(
    gap_a = map_dbl(rate, \(r) gap_of(cal$A, r)$pv_dkk),
    gap_b = map_dbl(rate, \(r) gap_of(cal$B, r)$pv_dkk),
    be_a = map2_dbl(gap_a, rate, \(g, r) breakeven_independent(
      g, r, params$age_ceiling, params$subaru_ceiling_km,
      params$increment_km, price_set(), params$discount_real)),
    be_b = map2_dbl(gap_b, rate, \(g, r) breakeven_independent(
      g, r, params$age_ceiling, params$subaru_ceiling_km,
      params$increment_km, price_set(), params$discount_real))
  )

be_tbl |>
  transmute(
    `Annual km` = fmt_km(rate),
    `Break-even independent, A` = paste0(fmt_dkk(be_a), " DKK"),
    `Break-even independent, B` = paste0(fmt_dkk(be_b), " DKK"),
    `Toyota small service` = paste0(fmt_dkk(params$service_toyota_small_dkk), " DKK"),
    `Ceiling pays at placeholder?` = ifelse(
      be_b < params$service_independent_small_dkk, "yes, on B", "no")
  ) |>
  show_table()
```

**These break-evens sit remarkably close to Toyota's own price.** At `r fmt_km(params$ref_rate)` km/yr an independent would have to charge `r fmt_dkk(be_tbl$be_b[be_tbl$rate == params$ref_rate])`–`r fmt_dkk(be_tbl$be_a[be_tbl$rate == params$ref_rate])` DKK for a small service — against Toyota's `r fmt_dkk(params$service_toyota_small_dkk)` — before the ceiling becomes worth keeping. In other words the independent has to be **barely cheaper than the franchised dealer** for the ceiling to pay, which is not what independents are for.

So if you would genuinely otherwise use an independent, the mileage ceiling does not repay the servicing needed to hold it. The remaining question is only how much cheaper your independent actually is, and a single quote settles it against the threshold above.

### 7.6 Holding period: when should you sell?

The gap window opens when Subaru's cover ends, at year `r fmt_num(my$term_subaru)` for a `r fmt_km(my$rate)` km/yr driver, and closes at the age ceiling in year `r fmt_num(my$term_toyota)`. Sell inside that window and the unused remainder is not destroyed — it is remaining cover the next owner inherits, and a rational used-car market pays for it. So the higher ceiling reaches you through two channels, and which one carries the value depends entirely on when you sell.

**Start from the case where holding period does not matter at all.** Viewed from today, the expected value you hand on is exactly the full gap value less the part you claim yourself, because you collect a resale premium only in the states where you have not already claimed. If the used market paid full actuarial value for remaining warranty, the two channels would sum to the same number at every sale date and the question would be empty.

Two frictions break that, and they pull in opposite directions:

1. **Capitalisation.** Used-car buyers do not pay full actuarial value for remaining warranty; the terms are not salient at the point of sale and are hard to verify. The parameter `resale_capitalisation`, set to `r fmt_pct(cap_default, 0)` here, is the share that does show up in the price. Anything below 100% penalises selling early.
2. **Compliance cost stops when you sell.** You pay only for the visits you make. Selling early avoids the later ones, which pushes the other way.

```{r resale-table}
holding_tbl |>
  filter(calib == "B") |>
  arrange(sale_year) |>
  transmute(
    `Sell in year` = fmt_num(sale_year, 0),
    `Claims you make` = fmt_dkk(captured_pv),
    `Cover handed on` = fmt_dkk(residual_pv),
    `Resale premium at sale` = fmt_dkk(wtp_at_sale),
    `Of which you capture` = fmt_dkk(resale_pv),
    `Upkeep you pay` = fmt_dkk(compliance_pv),
    `Net to you` = fmt_dkk(net_pv)
  ) |>
  show_table(caption = paste0(
    "Calibration B (adverse), ", fmt_km(my$rate), " km/yr, capitalisation ",
    fmt_pct(cap_default, 0),
    ". All figures are present values in today's DKK except the resale premium,",
    " which is stated in money of the sale year."
  ))
```

The **resale premium at sale** column is the directly checkable one: it is what the Toyota ought to fetch over the Subaru on the used market at that age, on account of battery warranty alone, conditional on neither car having claimed yet. If you can observe actual used-car pricing for the two models, that column is the number to test it against — and if the observed premium is far below it, that tells you capitalisation is low and you should hold rather than sell.

```{r fig-holding, fig.height=5.4}
hold_fine <- sort(unique(c(
  seq(1, params$age_ceiling, by = 0.25), my$term_subaru, my$hold
)))
hold_fine <- hold_fine[hold_fine > 0 & hold_fine <= params$age_ceiling]

hold_curves <- expand_grid(
  calib = names(cal), sale_year = hold_fine, cap = cap_share_grid
) |>
  pmap(\(calib, sale_year, cap) hold_value(calib, sale_year, cap)) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(
    lab = map_chr(calib, \(k) cal[[k]]$label),
    # Ordered by the number, not the string, or "100%" sorts before "30%".
    cap_lab = factor(
      paste0("capitalisation ", fmt_pct(capitalisation, 0)),
      levels = paste0("capitalisation ", fmt_pct(sort(cap_share_grid), 0))
    )
  )

marks <- hold_curves |>
  filter(abs(capitalisation - cap_default) < 1e-9,
         abs(sale_year - my$hold) < 1e-9)

ggplot(hold_curves, aes(sale_year, net_pv, colour = cap_lab)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = my$term_subaru, colour = pal[["subaru"]],
             linetype = "22", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.85) +
  geom_point(data = marks, colour = "black", size = 2.2) +
  facet_wrap(~lab, scales = "free_y") +
  annotate("text", x = my$term_subaru, y = Inf, label = " Subaru cover ends",
           hjust = 0, vjust = 1.6, size = 2.9, colour = pal[["subaru"]]) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_width(2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_comma()) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(
    c("#9ecae1", pal[["toyota"]], "#08306b")[seq_along(cap_share_grid)],
    paste0("capitalisation ", fmt_pct(sort(cap_share_grid), 0))
  )) +
  labs(
    title = "The net advantage of the Toyota over the Subaru, by the year you sell",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "At ", lab_km(my$rate), " km/yr",
      if (my$cost_faced <= 1) ", with no marginal servicing cost"
      else if (my$dealer) paste0(", net of the ", fmt_km(travel_extra_toyota_km),
                                 " km extra round trip to the Toyota workshop")
      else paste0(", net of Toyota servicing at ",
                  fmt_dkk(params$service_toyota_small_dkk), "/",
                  fmt_dkk(params$service_toyota_large_dkk), " DKK a visit")
    ),
    x = "Year you sell the car",
    y = "Toyota minus Subaru, net present value (DKK)",
    caption = paste0(
      "Black dot marks the ", fmt_num(my$hold, 0), "-year hold currently set. Each line fixes the share of remaining\n",
      "warranty value that the used-car market pays for. The value side alone is flat at 100%: what you do not\n",
      "claim you sell instead, so it does not matter when you sell. Any slope on that top line is therefore the\n",
      "servicing cost, which keeps accruing the longer you hold. Below 100% the value side rises with holding\n",
      "time as well, and the spread between the lines is the cost of imperfect transmission through resale."
    )
  ) +
  theme_note()
```

```{r holding-verdict, results='asis'}
# Everything here is stated relative to the plan currently set, with the sign
# carried explicitly: a positive delta means that sale date beats the plan.
b <- holding_tbl |> filter(calib == "B") |> arrange(sale_year)
cur <- b$net_pv[which.min(abs(b$sale_year - my$hold))]
b <- b |> mutate(delta = net_pv - cur)

best <- b |> slice_max(net_pv, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
early <- b |> filter(sale_year < my$hold)
material <- max(abs(b$delta)) > 1

cat(if (!my$binds) {
  paste0(
    "**The holding-period question does not arise for you.** At ",
    fmt_km(my$rate), " km/yr there is no gap between the two contracts at any ",
    "sale date, so the higher ceiling is worth nothing whenever you sell and ",
    "the timing of a sale cannot be argued from the battery warranty either way."
  )
} else if (!material) {
  paste0(
    "**The sale date barely matters.** Across every year considered the value ",
    "of the higher ceiling moves by under 1 DKK, because value you do not claim ",
    "you sell instead. Choose your holding period on other grounds."
  )
} else {
  paste0(
    "**For the ", fmt_num(my$hold, 0), "-year hold currently set: ",
    if (best$sale_year >= my$hold - 1e-9) {
      "holding to the end is the value-maximising choice."
    } else {
      paste0("selling in year ", fmt_num(best$sale_year, 0),
             " would be worth ", fmt_dkk(best$delta), " DKK more.")
    },
    "** ",
    if (my$cost_faced <= 1) paste0(
      "Because you face no marginal servicing cost, nothing pulls against ",
      "holding: every extra year converts cover the used market pays only ",
      fmt_pct(cap_default, 0), " for into cover you hold at full value. "
    ) else paste0(
      "There is a genuine trade-off here. Holding longer captures cover at full ",
      "value instead of selling it at ", fmt_pct(cap_default, 0),
      ", but it also means going on paying the ",
      fmt_dkk(my$cost_faced), " DKK of servicing difference, which accrues at ",
      fmt_num(my$rate / params$increment_km), " visits a year",
      if (my$dealer && subaru_placeholder) paste0(
        " — in your case entirely the ", fmt_km(travel_extra_toyota_km),
        " km of extra driving, since the two tariffs are set equal"
      ) else if (my$dealer) paste0(
        " — in your case the tariff difference plus the ",
        fmt_km(travel_extra_toyota_km), " km of extra driving"
      ) else "", ". "
    ),
    if (nrow(early) > 0) paste0(
      "Selling earlier than planned changes the value by ",
      rng(range(early$delta)), " DKK on the adverse calibration, ",
      "against a full gap value of ", fmt_dkk(max(my$gap_full)),
      " DKK. On the benign calibration the same range is ",
      rng(range({
        a2 <- holding_tbl |> filter(calib == "A") |> arrange(sale_year)
        cur_a <- a2$net_pv[which.min(abs(a2$sale_year - my$hold))]
        a2$net_pv[a2$sale_year < my$hold] - cur_a
      })), " DKK. ",
      if (max(abs(early$delta)) < 0.1 * params$severity_buyer_dkk) paste0(
        "Either way the amount at stake in the *timing* is small next to the ",
        fmt_dkk(params$severity_buyer_dkk), " DKK the cover insures against, so ",
        "**the sale date is not something to plan the purchase around** — and ",
        "the warranty is not a reason to keep a car you would otherwise replace."
      ) else paste0(
        "That is large enough to be worth planning around: if an early sale is ",
        "likely, weigh it before paying anything for the mileage ceiling."
      )
    ) else ""
  )
})
```

### 7.7 What if you drive more than you expect?

Nobody knows their future annual mileage to the nearest thousand kilometres, and this contract is unusually sensitive to it: everything is zero below `r fmt_km(gap_opens_at)` km/yr and rises steeply above. So the useful question is not "what is it worth at my expected mileage" but "what does it cost me to be wrong about my mileage".

```{r usage-compare}
u_lo <- params$my_rate_compare
u_hi <- params$my_rate
u_rates <- sort(unique(c(u_lo, u_hi)))

usage_tbl <- expand_grid(rate = u_rates, calib = names(cal)) |>
  mutate(
    gap = map2_dbl(calib, rate, \(k, r) gap_of(cal[[k]], r)$pv_dkk),
    cost_ind = map_dbl(rate, \(r) cost_of(r, dealer_anyway = FALSE)$pv_dkk),
    cost_dlr = map_dbl(rate, \(r) cost_of(r, dealer_anyway = TRUE)$pv_dkk),
    sub_ends = pmin(params$age_ceiling, params$subaru_ceiling_km / rate)
  )

usage_tbl |>
  transmute(
    `Annual km` = fmt_km(rate),
    Calibration = calib,
    `Subaru cover ends` = paste0("yr ", fmt_num(sub_ends)),
    `Gap value` = paste0(fmt_dkk(gap), " DKK"),
    `Net, independent` = paste0(fmt_dkk(gap - cost_ind), " DKK"),
    `Net, dealer anyway` = paste0(fmt_dkk(gap - cost_dlr), " DKK")
  ) |>
  show_table()
```

```{r usage-marginal, include=FALSE}
step <- 1000
marg <- tibble(rate = seq(gap_opens_at, max(u_rates) * 1.4, by = step)) |>
  mutate(
    gap_b = map_dbl(rate, \(r) gap_of(cal$B, r)$pv_dkk),
    d_gap = (gap_b - lag(gap_b))
  )

gap_at <- \(r, k) gap_of(cal[[k]], r)$pv_dkk
overshoot <- \(r) map_dbl(names(cal), \(k) gap_at(r, k)) |> set_names(names(cal))

o_hi <- overshoot(u_hi)
o_lo <- overshoot(u_lo)
```

```{r usage-prose, results='asis'}
in_band <- marg$d_gap[marg$rate > min(u_rates) & marg$rate <= max(u_rates)]
slope <- if (length(in_band) > 0 && any(is.finite(in_band))) {
  mean(in_band, na.rm = TRUE)
} else {
  NA_real_
}

cat(if (length(u_rates) < 2) {
  paste0(
    "`my_rate_compare` is set to the same figure as `my_rate`, so there is ",
    "nothing to compare. Set it to a different rate — the ", fmt_km(gap_opens_at),
    " km/yr kink is the natural choice — to see what your mileage uncertainty ",
    "is worth."
  )
} else if (max(u_rates) <= gap_opens_at) {
  paste0(
    "Both rates compared here sit at or below the ", fmt_km(gap_opens_at),
    " km/yr kink, so the ceiling is worth exactly zero at either. The question ",
    "only becomes live if your usage turns out higher than both."
  )
} else paste0(
  "At ", fmt_km(u_lo), " km/yr the two contracts are ",
  if (max(o_lo) < 1) "exactly identical" else paste0("worth ", rng(o_lo), " DKK apart"),
  ". At ", fmt_km(u_hi), " km/yr the ceiling is worth ", rng(o_hi), " DKK. ",
  "**So the value of the Toyota ceiling to you is created almost entirely by the ",
  fmt_km(abs(u_hi - u_lo)), " km/yr between those two figures**",
  if (is.finite(slope)) paste0(
    ", and it is created steeply: each additional 1,000 km/yr over that stretch ",
    "adds roughly ", fmt_dkk(slope), " DKK on the adverse calibration."
  ) else "."
))
```

```{r fig-usage, fig.height=4.8}
u_seq <- seq(gap_opens_at * 0.75, max(u_rates) * 1.5, length.out = 140)

u_curves <- expand_grid(calib = names(cal), r = u_seq) |>
  mutate(
    gap = map2_dbl(calib, r, \(k, rr) gap_of(cal[[k]], rr)$pv_dkk),
    lab = map_chr(calib, \(k) cal[[k]]$label)
  )

u_marks <- tibble(
  r = u_rates,
  what = c(paste0("compare: ", lab_km(u_lo)), paste0("your estimate: ", lab_km(u_hi)))
) |>
  mutate(
    gap = map_dbl(r, \(x) gap_at(x, "B")),
    # A point sitting on the axis has no room for a label below it.
    vj = ifelse(gap < max(u_curves$gap) * 0.08, -1.1, 1.7)
  )

ggplot(u_curves, aes(r, gap, colour = lab)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = u_lo, xmax = u_hi, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = pal[["neutral"]], alpha = 0.10) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = u_marks, aes(r, gap), inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 2.4) +
  geom_text(data = u_marks, aes(r, gap, label = what, vjust = vj),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = -0.06, size = 2.9, colour = "grey25") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(c(pal[["A"]], pal[["B"]]),
                                        map_chr(names(cal), \(k) cal[[k]]$label))) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = lab_km) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_comma()) +
  labs(
    title = "The cost of being wrong about your own mileage",
    subtitle = paste0("Gross gap value against realised usage. Shaded: the stretch between ",
                      lab_km(u_lo), " and ", lab_km(u_hi), " km/yr"),
    x = "Usage rate you actually turn out to drive (km/yr)",
    y = "Gross value of the ceiling (DKK)",
    caption = paste0(
      "Everything left of ", lab_km(gap_opens_at), " km/yr is exactly zero: below the kink the two contracts are the same\n",
      "contract. The curve is convex just above it, so the risk is asymmetric — driving 5,000 km/yr less than you\n",
      "expect costs you little, while driving 5,000 more than you expect gains you more than proportionally.\n",
      "If your mileage is uncertain, that asymmetry is itself a mild argument for the higher ceiling."
    )
  ) +
  theme_note()
```

The asymmetry is real, but it is not free. Below `r fmt_km(gap_opens_at)` km/yr the gap value is identically zero, and the *number* of visits each owner must make at their own dealer is identical too, because Subaru's cover also lasts the full `r params$age_ceiling` years at those rates. What does not vanish is the journey: the Toyota workshop stays `r fmt_km(travel_extra_toyota_km)` km further away whatever your mileage, which is why the table above shows a cost of `r fmt_dkk(abs(usage_tbl$cost_dlr[1]))` DKK even at `r fmt_km(u_lo)` km/yr against a gap of zero. **So overestimating your mileage is not costless** — you would have bought cover you turned out not to need, and driven further to keep it.

Underestimating is the expensive direction, and more than proportionally so, because the curve is convex through this range. A buyer genuinely uncertain between `r fmt_km(u_lo)` and `r fmt_km(u_hi)` km/yr should therefore weight the ceiling nearer the upper figure than the midpoint — though on these numbers the whole quantity in dispute is still small.

### 7.8 Your decision, worked

```{r my-decision}
tibble(
  Quantity = c(
    "Usage rate assumed",
    "Years you keep the car",
    "Subaru cover ends",
    "Toyota cover ends",
    "Extra dealer visits required",
    "Gross value of the higher ceiling",
    "Value realised before you sell",
    "Compliance cost you would face",
    "Net value of the ceiling",
    "Break-even independent price"
  ),
  Value = c(
    paste0(fmt_km(my$rate), " km/yr"),
    paste0(fmt_num(my$hold, 0), " yr"),
    paste0("year ", fmt_num(my$term_subaru)),
    paste0("year ", fmt_num(my$term_toyota)),
    fmt_num(my$extra_visits, 0),
    paste0(rng(my$gap_full), " DKK"),
    paste0(rng(my$gap_held), " DKK"),
    paste0(fmt_dkk(my$cost_faced), " DKK",
           if (my$dealer) " (dealer either way; tariff gap plus travel)" else ""),
    paste0(rng(my$net), " DKK"),
    if (my$binds && all(is.finite(my$be_ind))) {
      paste0(rng(my$be_ind), " DKK, small service")
    } else "n/a"
  )
) |>
  show_table(align = "lr")
```

```{r my-verdict, results='asis'}
cat(if (!my$binds) {
  paste0(
    "**The two contracts are identical for you.** At ", fmt_km(my$rate),
    " km/yr you never reach Subaru's ", fmt_km(params$subaru_ceiling_km),
    " km ceiling inside the ", params$age_ceiling,
    "-year age limit, so there is nothing to value. Choose on other grounds, ",
    "and do not pay anything for the mileage ceiling."
  )
} else if (min(my$net) > 0) {
  paste0(
    "**The ceiling pays for you on both calibrations.** Net of the ",
    fmt_dkk(my$cost_faced), " DKK of servicing difference you would face, it is ",
    "worth ", rng(my$net), " DKK, plus the resale and documentation value in ",
    "section 7.3. Section 7.10 shows how to keep that value for less by ",
    "returning to the dealer only when Subaru's cover would have run out."
  )
} else if (max(my$net) > 0) {
  paste0(
    "**The ceiling pays only on the adverse calibration.** Against ",
    fmt_dkk(my$cost_faced), " DKK of servicing difference",
    if (my$dealer) paste0(
      " — which in your case is entirely the ", fmt_km(travel_extra_toyota_km),
      " km of extra driving, since Subaru's tariff is a placeholder set equal ",
      "to Toyota's —"
    ) else "",
    " the gap is worth ", rng(my$gap_full), " DKK, so the net runs from ",
    rng(my$net), " DKK. It turns on which fade scenario holds, which is the ",
    "one thing no quote can settle. Two considerations pull towards taking it ",
    "anyway: a warranty is a variance-reduction purchase rather than an ",
    "expected-value one (section 1.2), and the resale and documentation ",
    "channels (section 7.3) are not counted above. Section 7.10 shows how to ",
    "cut the servicing side without giving up the cover."
  )
} else {
  paste0(
    "**On expected value the ceiling does not pay for you.** The servicing ",
    "difference of ", fmt_dkk(my$cost_faced), " DKK exceeds the ",
    rng(my$gap_full), " DKK of cover on both calibrations",
    if (all(is.finite(my$be_ind))) paste0(
      "; it would only pay if an independent charged more than ",
      rng(my$be_ind), " DKK for a small service, against Toyota's ",
      fmt_dkk(params$service_toyota_small_dkk)
    ) else "",
    ". Two caveats pull the other way and are not in that arithmetic: a ",
    "warranty is a variance-reduction purchase rather than an expected-value ",
    "one, so a risk-averse buyer should pay something above the expected value ",
    "(section 1.2); and the resale and documentation channels (section 7.3) ",
    "are plausibly larger than the claim value itself. Neither is large enough ",
    "to close a gap of this size, but both narrow it."
  )
})
```

### 7.9 What if the pack costs more than assumed?

Every figure in section 7 scales linearly in the buyer-side severity, which makes this the cleanest sensitivity in the note — and, given that the figure is a judgement rather than a quote (section 1.1), the most important one.

```{r severity-sensitivity}
sev_grid <- num(params$severity_buyer_sensitivity)

expand_grid(severity = sev_grid, calib = names(cal)) |>
  mutate(
    gap = map2_dbl(calib, severity,
                   \(k, s) gap_of(cal[[k]], my$rate, severity = s)$pv_dkk),
    net_ind = gap - my$cost[["independent"]],
    net_dlr = gap - my$cost[["dealer"]]
  ) |>
  transmute(
    `Buyer-side severity` = paste0(fmt_dkk(severity), " DKK"),
    `vs default` = paste0(fmt_num(severity / params$severity_buyer_dkk, 1), "x"),
    Calibration = calib,
    `Gap value` = paste0(fmt_dkk(gap), " DKK"),
    `Net, independent` = paste0(fmt_dkk(net_ind), " DKK"),
    `Net, dealer anyway` = paste0(fmt_dkk(net_dlr), " DKK")
  ) |>
  show_table(caption = paste0("At ", fmt_km(my$rate), " km/yr, ",
                              fmt_num(my$hold, 0), "-year hold"))
```

```{r severity-breakeven, include=FALSE}
# Severity at which the ceiling clears in the independent-workshop scenario.
sev_unit <- map_dbl(names(cal), \(k) gap_of(cal[[k]], my$rate, severity = 1)$pv_dkk) |>
  set_names(names(cal))
sev_be <- ifelse(sev_unit > 0, my$cost[["independent"]] / sev_unit, NA_real_) |>
  set_names(names(cal))
# The same break-even under the scenario the buyer says applies to them.
sev_be_faced <- ifelse(sev_unit > 0, my$cost_faced / sev_unit, NA_real_) |>
  set_names(names(cal))
```

```{r severity-verdict, results='asis'}
mult <- sev_be / params$severity_buyer_dkk
plausible <- 3  # beyond about 3x the trade figure, no retail bill is credible

cat(if (!my$binds || !is.finite(mult[["B"]])) {
  paste0(
    "At ", fmt_km(my$rate), " km/yr there is no gap to value, so severity ",
    "scales nothing: the ceiling is worth zero at any pack price. The ",
    "sensitivity above matters only once your usage passes ",
    fmt_km(gap_opens_at), " km/yr."
  )
} else paste0(
  "Raising severity narrows the shortfall but does not close it quickly. In the ",
  "independent-workshop scenario the ceiling would only clear at a buyer-side ",
  "severity of ", fmt_dkk(sev_be[["B"]]), " DKK on the adverse calibration — ",
  fmt_num(mult[["B"]], 1), "x the default, which is high but not absurd for a ",
  "retail pack with VAT. On the benign calibration it would take ",
  fmt_num(mult[["A"]], 0), "x, which no realistic Danish invoice reaches. ",
  if (mult[["B"]] > plausible) paste0(
    "So on these servicing assumptions, correcting the severity error alone ",
    "does not rescue the ceiling for a buyer using an independent workshop; it ",
    "would take a higher severity *and* a lower dealer premium together."
  ) else paste0(
    "So a realistic retail severity could on its own flip the verdict in the ",
    "adverse scenario, which is reason enough to get the quote."
  ),
  if (my$cost[["dealer"]] <= 0) paste0(
    " In the franchised-dealer scenario the ceiling clears at any severity, ",
    "because under equal premiums the cost it is weighed against is zero."
  ) else paste0(
    " In the franchised-dealer scenario the cost to beat is only ",
    fmt_dkk(my$cost[["dealer"]]), " DKK, and the break-even severity there is ",
    fmt_dkk(sev_be_faced[["B"]]), " DKK on the adverse calibration — against the ",
    fmt_dkk(params$severity_buyer_dkk),
    " DKK set. **On that scenario the decision sits almost exactly on the ",
    "knife edge**, which is why a real quote for an out-of-warranty replacement ",
    "would settle more than any other single number here."
  )
))
```

---

### 7.10 Servicing strategy: you are not choosing for ten years at once

The note has so far treated dealer-versus-independent as a single decision covering the whole term. It is not. Two features of the contract make it a question about *which visits*:

1. **The base guarantee is unconditional.** Cover runs to `r params$base_years` yr / `r fmt_km(params$base_km)` km without any health check. At `r fmt_km(my$rate)` km/yr you reach `r fmt_km(params$base_km)` km in year **`r fmt_num(params$base_km / my$rate)`**. Health checks buy coverage only beyond that point.
2. **Cover is reinstatable** (section 3.3). A gap in dealer servicing suspends the guarantee rather than destroying it, so an owner can use an independent early and return later.

Together these allow a mixed strategy: independent up to `dealer_from_year`, franchised dealer after. The parameter applies to both cars, so it is the strategy being priced, not a handicap applied to one make.

```{r strategy-table}
d_grid <- sort(unique(c(num(params$dealer_from_grid), params$dealer_from_year)))
d_grid <- d_grid[d_grid >= 0 & d_grid <= params$age_ceiling]

t_base_yr <- params$base_km / my$rate

strategy <- expand_grid(dealer_from = d_grid, calib = names(cal)) |>
  mutate(
    toy_spend = map_dbl(dealer_from, \(d) cost_of(
      my$rate, dealer_anyway = my$dealer, dealer_from = d)$pv_toyota),
    gap = map2_dbl(calib, dealer_from,
                   \(k, d) gap_of(cal[[k]], my$rate, dealer_from = d)$pv_dkk),
    exposed = map2_dbl(calib, dealer_from, \(k, d) suspended_exposure(
      my$rate, cal[[k]]$a, cal[[k]]$b, cal[[k]]$sd_unit, d_crit,
      params$age_ceiling, params$base_km, d, params$severity_buyer_dkk,
      params$severity_decline, params$discount_real, params$repair_worthy)$pv_dkk),
    visits_dealer = map_dbl(dealer_from, \(d) cost_of(
      my$rate, dealer_anyway = my$dealer, dealer_from = d)$visits_at_toyota)
  )

strategy |>
  filter(calib == "B") |>
  arrange(dealer_from) |>
  transmute(
    `Dealer from year` = fmt_num(dealer_from, 0),
    `Visits at Toyota` = fmt_num(visits_dealer, 0),
    `Your servicing spend` = paste0(fmt_dkk(toy_spend), " DKK"),
    `Saved vs always-dealer` = paste0(
      fmt_dkk(toy_spend[dealer_from == 0][1] - toy_spend), " DKK"),
    `Gap value kept` = paste0(fmt_dkk(gap), " DKK"),
    `Own cover given up` = paste0(fmt_dkk(exposed), " DKK")
  ) |>
  show_table(caption = paste0(
    "Calibration B (adverse) at ", fmt_km(my$rate),
    " km/yr. Spend is the present value of your own servicing on the Toyota, ",
    "including travel. Base cover runs unconditionally to year ",
    fmt_num(t_base_yr), "; Subaru's ceiling falls in year ",
    fmt_num(my$term_subaru), "."
  ))
```

```{r strategy-reads, include=FALSE}
s0 <- strategy |> filter(calib == "B", dealer_from == 0)
# Latest start that costs nothing in gap value, to the nearest grid point.
free_start <- strategy |>
  filter(calib == "B", gap >= 0.999 * s0$gap) |>
  slice_max(dealer_from, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
```

Before reading the columns, note the scale of the first one. Holding Toyota cover for the full term costs **`r fmt_dkk(s0$toy_spend)` DKK** of servicing in present value, to protect a contract gap worth `r fmt_dkk(s0$gap)` DKK on the adverse calibration. The upkeep is more than an order of magnitude larger than the thing it is buying. That is not an argument against servicing the car — you would service it anyway — but it is decisive about how much of that spend should be attributed to the *warranty*.

**Delaying costs nothing until Subaru's cover runs out.** The gap is the window where Toyota covers and Subaru does not, so it cannot open before year `r fmt_num(my$term_subaru)` whatever you do. Returning to the dealer by then keeps the entire gap value while cutting your Toyota visits from `r fmt_num(s0$visits_dealer, 0)` to `r fmt_num(free_start$visits_dealer, 0)` — a saving of **`r fmt_dkk(s0$toy_spend - free_start$toy_spend)` DKK** on the servicing bill for no loss in the contract comparison at all. Delay past that point and the gap itself starts to shrink.

**What you give up is your own cover, not the comparison.** Between year `r fmt_num(t_base_yr)` and your return to the dealer, neither car is covered — that is the last column, and it is a genuine cost that cancels out of the Toyota-versus-Subaru arithmetic while remaining entirely real to you. On the adverse calibration a return in year `r fmt_num(free_start$dealer_from, 0)` exposes you to `r fmt_dkk(free_start$exposed)` DKK of uninsured crossing risk.

Two cautions before acting on this. The strategy depends on the reinstatement reading, which section 3.3 flags as inferred rather than stated for the battery. And it says nothing about **Toyota Relax**, the whole-vehicle extended warranty, which is genuinely sequential — it extends 12 months per service, so gaps break the chain. At your mileage Relax is limited anyway: its `r fmt_km(185000)` km cap arrives in year `r fmt_num(185000 / my$rate)`, so it is a low-mileage product that you would exhaust well before the age ceiling regardless.

#### The drive to the workshop

```{r travel-table}
per_visit_extra <- travel_extra_toyota_km * params$travel_cost_dkk_per_km

tibble(cost_per_km = num(params$travel_cost_sensitivity)) |>
  mutate(
    always = map_dbl(cost_per_km, \(c) cost_of(
      my$rate, dealer_anyway = my$dealer, prices = price_set(per_km = c),
      dealer_from = 0)$pv_dkk),
    delayed = map_dbl(cost_per_km, \(c) cost_of(
      my$rate, dealer_anyway = my$dealer, prices = price_set(per_km = c),
      dealer_from = free_start$dealer_from)$pv_dkk)
  ) |>
  transmute(
    `Cost per km` = paste0(fmt_num(cost_per_km, 2), " DKK"),
    `Extra per Toyota visit` = paste0(
      fmt_dkk(travel_extra_toyota_km * cost_per_km), " DKK"),
    `Servicing differential, dealer from new` = paste0(fmt_dkk(always), " DKK"),
    !!paste0("Differential, dealer from year ",
             fmt_num(free_start$dealer_from, 0)) := paste0(fmt_dkk(delayed), " DKK")
  ) |>
  show_table(caption = paste0(
    "The Toyota dealer is ", fmt_km(travel_extra_toyota_km),
    " km further, round trip, than the Subaru dealer."
  ))
```

```{r travel-prose, results='asis'}
extra <- travel_extra_toyota_km
per_visit <- abs(extra) * params$travel_cost_dkk_per_km
visits_yr <- my$rate / params$increment_km
hours_yr <- abs(extra) * visits_yr / 60
mean_price <- mean(c(params$service_toyota_small_dkk, params$service_toyota_large_dkk))
dealer_only <- cost_of(my$rate, dealer_anyway = TRUE, dealer_from = 0)$pv_dkk

cat(if (abs(extra) < 1) {
  paste0(
    "The two workshops are equidistant on the figures set, so travel drops out ",
    "of the comparison entirely. If that is not right, set the round-trip ",
    "distances in the parameter block: the difference is worth about ",
    fmt_dkk(10 * params$travel_cost_dkk_per_km * visits_yr),
    " DKK over the term for every 10 km of asymmetry."
  )
} else {
  nearer <- if (extra > 0) "Toyota" else "Subaru"
  further <- if (extra > 0) "Subaru" else "Toyota"
  paste0(
    "The ", nearer, " workshop is ", fmt_km(abs(extra)),
    " km further round trip than the ", further, " one, which at ",
    fmt_num(params$travel_cost_dkk_per_km, 2), " DKK per km adds ",
    fmt_dkk(per_visit), " DKK to every ", nearer, " visit — about ",
    fmt_pct(per_visit / mean_price, 0), " on top of the service price. At ",
    fmt_num(visits_yr), " visits a year that is roughly ", fmt_num(hours_yr, 1),
    " hours a year of extra driving. The per-km figure is a judgement, not a ",
    "quote: set it to cover energy, tyres and wear, plus whatever you put on ",
    "that time.\n\n",
    "**This matters more than it first appears, because it is the one thing ",
    "that breaks the tie.** If you would use a franchised dealer regardless, ",
    "and the two tariffs turn out equal, the servicing differential would be ",
    "exactly zero — the two makes cancelling. They do not cancel once distance ",
    "is counted: on these figures the extra journeys alone come to **",
    fmt_dkk(abs(dealer_only)), " DKK** over the term, ",
    if (extra > 0) "against you" else "in your favour",
    ", which is of the same order as the entire gap value of ",
    rng(my$gap_full), " DKK. A ", fmt_km(abs(extra)),
    " km detour, ", fmt_num(visits_yr), " times a year for ",
    params$age_ceiling, " years, is not a detail."
  )
})
```

An independent closer to home would save on both counts at once, which is why the two decisions interact: **the case for an independent is strongest in exactly the years when the cover is worth least**, and that is the period the strategy above already hands to them.

---

## 8. Why the million kilometres is cheap: the self-financing argument

Section 4 gives one explanation for the low cost of Toyota's ceiling: it sits above $x_{\text{crit}}$, so it censors nothing, so it costs nothing. That holds, but it is the weaker of the two available explanations. The stronger one follows from the increment rule.

Every `r fmt_km(params$increment_km)` km of coverage is purchased with a dealer visit. Riding the coverage to the ceiling requires `r fmt_num(checks_to_toyota, 0)` visits. At a gross margin of `r fmt_dkk(params$service_margin_low)`–`r fmt_dkk(params$service_margin_high)` DKK per visit, that is **`r fmt_dkk(checks_to_toyota * params$service_margin_low)`–`r fmt_dkk(checks_to_toyota * params$service_margin_high)` DKK of service margin against a `r fmt_dkk(params$severity_maker_dkk)` DKK pack**. Subaru's `r fmt_km(params$subaru_ceiling_km)` km ceiling generates `r fmt_num(checks_to_subaru, 0)` visits, or `r fmt_dkk(checks_to_subaru * params$service_margin_low)`–`r fmt_dkk(checks_to_subaru * params$service_margin_high)` DKK.

```{r service-margin}
tibble(
  Make = c("Toyota", "Subaru"),
  ceiling = c(params$toyota_ceiling_km, params$subaru_ceiling_km)
) |>
  mutate(
    visits = checks_required(ceiling, params$base_km, params$increment_km,
                             from_zero = TRUE),
    `Mileage ceiling` = fmt_km(ceiling),
    `Visits from zero` = fmt_num(visits, 0),
    `Margin @ low (DKK)` = fmt_dkk(visits * params$service_margin_low),
    `Margin @ high (DKK)` = fmt_dkk(visits * params$service_margin_high),
    `Cover ratio vs pack` = paste0(
      fmt_num(visits * params$service_margin_low / params$severity_maker_dkk, 2), "–",
      fmt_num(visits * params$service_margin_high / params$severity_maker_dkk, 2), "x"
    )
  ) |>
  select(Make, `Mileage ceiling`, `Visits from zero`, `Margin @ low (DKK)`,
         `Margin @ high (DKK)`, `Cover ratio vs pack`) |>
  show_table()
```

Three consequences:

1. **The warranty is not a net liability.** It is a service subscription with a guarantee attached. The customer funds the reserve, and at the upper end of the margin range the programme is cash-positive against a *certain* claim, not merely a probable one.
2. **The ceiling is a throughput target, not a risk parameter.** Raising it from 650,000 to `r fmt_km(params$toyota_ceiling_km)` km adds `r fmt_num((params$toyota_ceiling_km - 650000) / params$increment_km, 0)` potential service visits per high-mileage customer. Read as a service-network revenue instrument, the number is legible; read as a statement about cell chemistry, it is not.
3. **The lapse mechanism and the revenue mechanism are the same mechanism.** Every missed visit simultaneously terminates coverage and forgoes margin, so the programme is self-limiting in exactly the population that costs most.

This also disposes of the puzzle in section 7.2. Adverse selection is less dangerous than it looks, because the high-mileage customers who extract the most from the contract are the same ones who pay the most into it, at a rate proportional to their usage. The contract is close to usage-priced by construction.

---

## 9. Using this in a negotiation

The manufacturer-side arithmetic in sections 6 and 8 is not just background. It tells a buyer what each side of the table is actually protecting, which is the useful thing to know before discussing price.

```{r negotiation-numbers}
tibble(
  Quantity = c(
    "What the extra coverage costs Toyota to grant, per car sold",
    "What it is worth to you, gross",
    "What Toyota's service programme earns if you comply to the ceiling",
    "Cost of one pack replacement"
  ),
  Amount = c(
    paste0(rng(decomp$total * params$severity_maker_dkk), " DKK"),
    if (my$binds) paste0(rng(my$gap_full), " DKK") else "0 DKK",
    paste0(rng(checks_to_toyota *
                 c(params$service_margin_low, params$service_margin_high)),
           " DKK"),
    paste0(fmt_dkk(params$severity_maker_dkk), " DKK")
  ),
  Source = c("Section 6.3", "Section 7.8", "Section 8", "Section 1")
) |>
  show_table(align = "lrl")
```

Four things follow.

1. **Do not pay a meaningful premium for the mileage ceiling.** It costs Toyota `r fmt_dkk(decomp$total[1] * params$severity_maker_dkk)`–`r fmt_dkk(decomp$total[2] * params$severity_maker_dkk)` DKK per car sold to grant — an accrual, not a cost they feel per sale. A salesperson presenting the million kilometres as a major concession is describing something that is close to free to give. If it is being priced into the car at more than a few thousand DKK, that is not what it is worth.

2. **Their real interest is the service stream, so negotiate there.** The `r fmt_num(checks_to_toyota, 0)` visits needed to ride the coverage to the ceiling are worth `r fmt_dkk(checks_to_toyota * params$service_margin_low)`–`r fmt_dkk(checks_to_toyota * params$service_margin_high)` DKK of gross margin, `r fmt_num(checks_to_toyota * params$service_margin_low / params$severity_maker_dkk, 1)`–`r fmt_num(checks_to_toyota * params$service_margin_high / params$severity_maker_dkk, 1)`× the price of the pack they are guaranteeing. The concession worth asking for is therefore **a capped or prepaid service price**, not a discount on the car. A prepaid plan at close to independent-workshop rates converts the ceiling from something that costs you `r fmt_dkk(my$cost_full)` DKK to hold into something close to free — which, per section 7.5, is the entire decision.

3. **The ceiling is not a quality signal, so do not pay for reassurance.** Two firms building the same pack chose ceilings a factor of `r fmt_num(params$toyota_ceiling_km / params$subaru_ceiling_km, 0)` apart (section 10). Whatever generates that spread, it is not a difference of belief about the cells. If a longer warranty is being sold to you as evidence of a better battery, the comparison refutes it directly: the battery is the same battery.

4. **Symmetrically, Subaru's shorter ceiling is cheap for them to extend.** Moving from `r fmt_km(params$subaru_ceiling_km)` to `r fmt_km(400000)` km would cost them roughly `r fmt_dkk((cap_table$claims_a[cap_table$cap_km == 400000] - cap_table$claims_a[cap_table$cap_km == params$subaru_ceiling_km]) * params$severity_maker_dkk)`–`r fmt_dkk((cap_table$claims_b[cap_table$cap_km == 400000] - cap_table$claims_b[cap_table$cap_km == params$subaru_ceiling_km]) * params$severity_maker_dkk)` DKK per car in expected claims. If you are a high-mileage buyer and Subaru is otherwise the better car, an extended-mileage clause is a cheaper thing for a dealer to concede than an equivalent cash discount — and worth asking for in writing.

> **A caution on all four.** These are arguments about what the *warranty difference* is worth. They say nothing about which car is better, and the mileage ceiling is a small term in a purchase this size. Use them to stop the warranty being oversold, not as the basis of the decision.

---

## 10. What can be inferred about the failure rate

Very little — and the increment mechanism sharpens the point rather than weakening it.

A single announced warranty term is one scalar emitted by an optimisation with many free parameters: severity, compliance rate, service margin, discount rate, competitive positioning, residual-value and lease-book support. The system is badly underdetermined; the hazard is not identified by the contract.

The decisive evidence: **two firms with the same cells, the same pack, the same threshold, the same base term and the same increment rule have chosen mileage ceilings differing by a factor of `r fmt_num(params$toyota_ceiling_km / params$subaru_ceiling_km, 0)`, producing `r fmt_num(uncapped[["A"]] / cap_table$claims_a[cap_table$cap_km == params$subaru_ceiling_km], 0)`x and `r fmt_num(uncapped[["B"]] / cap_table$claims_b[cap_table$cap_km == params$subaru_ceiling_km], 1)`x differences in expected claims** on the benign and adverse calibrations respectively. The engineering belief is common; the contracts are not. Whatever generates the spread, it is not the failure distribution. If anything, Subaru declining to follow on identical hardware is mild evidence *against* reading Toyota's number as a confidence signal — had fade data been the binding input, one would expect convergence.

What *would* identify the failure distribution: warranty accrual per unit from the financial statements; **claims development triangles** by sale cohort and months in service — the standard actuarial data layout, a matrix with one row per cohort of cars sold and one column per elapsed month, whose cells hold claims paid to date, so that reading across a row traces how a single cohort's claims emerge over time and reading down a column compares cohorts at equal maturity; and fleet SoH telemetry.

Note also that the informational content sits in the **threshold**, not the distance. If mean fade at 10 years is ~15% with cross-sectional sigma ~4%, a 30-point threshold sits at $z \approx 3.75$ (claim rate ~$10^{-4}$) while a 20-point threshold sits at $z \approx 1.25$ (~10%). A ten-point shift moves expected claims by three orders of magnitude. That asymmetry is precisely why the mileage ceiling can be inflated freely.

---

## 11. Open questions and model weaknesses

### 11.1 Sensitivity ranking

The two financial parameters that scale the PV enter with near-identical leverage but wildly different uncertainty.

```{r elasticity}
t_ref <- buyer_gap |>
  filter(rate == params$ref_rate, calib == "A") |>
  pull(t_bar)

span_decline <- 100 * (max(decline_grid) - min(decline_grid))
span_discount <- 100 * (max(discount_cred) - min(discount_cred))

tibble(
  Parameter = c(
    paste0("Severity decline δ (at ", fmt_pct(params$severity_decline, 0), ")"),
    paste0("Real discount r (at ", fmt_pct(params$discount_real, 0), ")")
  ),
  `d lnPV / d param` = c(
    fmt_num(-t_ref / (1 - params$severity_decline), 2),
    fmt_num(-t_ref / (1 + params$discount_real), 2)
  ),
  `PV multiple per -1pp` = c(
    paste0(fmt_num(exp(t_ref / (1 - params$severity_decline) * 0.01), 2), "x"),
    paste0(fmt_num(exp(t_ref / (1 + params$discount_real) * 0.01), 2), "x")
  ),
  `Credible range` = c(
    paste0(fmt_pct(min(decline_grid), 0), "–", fmt_pct(max(decline_grid), 0),
           " (", fmt_num(span_decline, 0), " pp)"),
    paste0(fmt_pct(min(discount_cred), 0), "–", fmt_pct(max(discount_cred), 0),
           " (", fmt_num(span_discount, 0), " pp)")
  )
) |>
  show_table(align = "lrrr")
```

Evaluated at $\bar{t} = `r fmt_num(t_ref, 2)`$ the two elasticities are almost the same, so per percentage point they move the answer by almost the same factor. The ranges are not. The credible range for $\delta$ spans `r fmt_num(span_decline, 0)` percentage points (`r fmt_pct(min(decline_grid), 0)`–`r fmt_pct(max(decline_grid), 0)`) against `r fmt_num(span_discount, 0)` pp for the real discount rate (`r fmt_pct(min(discount_cred), 0)`–`r fmt_pct(max(discount_cred), 0)`; the `r fmt_pct(max(discount_grid), 0)` column in section 7.1 is shown only to demonstrate insensitivity, not as a defensible value). **$\delta$ therefore carries roughly `r fmt_num(span_decline / span_discount, 0)` times the uncertainty at the same leverage**, and it is the parameter that deserves the attention that discount-rate debates usually absorb.

```{r decline-sensitivity}
expand_grid(calib = names(cal), decline = decline_grid) |>
  mutate(pv = map2_dbl(calib, decline,
                       \(k, d) gap_of(cal[[k]], params$ref_rate, decline = d)$pv_dkk)) |>
  mutate(`Severity decline` = fmt_pct(decline, 0)) |>
  select(`Severity decline`, calib, pv) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = calib, values_from = pv,
              names_prefix = "PV, calibration ") |>
  mutate(across(starts_with("PV"), \(x) fmt_dkk(x))) |>
  show_table(align = "lrr",
             caption = paste0("Gap PV at ", fmt_km(params$ref_rate),
                              " km/yr, real discount ",
                              fmt_pct(params$discount_real, 0)))
```

### 11.2 Remaining weaknesses

1. **Separability of $b$ in $r$.** The model assumes the throughput coefficient is independent of usage rate. It almost certainly is not: high-mileage drivers DC-fast-charge more, run wider SoC windows, and spend more time at elevated cell temperature. If $b = b(r)$ is increasing, $x_{\text{crit}}$ shrinks in the usage tail — a 100,000 km/yr taxi might cross `r fmt_pct(params$soh_threshold, 0)` at 300,000 km rather than `r fmt_km(params$cal_a_km_crit_pure)` — pulling the bite point down and giving the mileage cap a genuine actuarial rationale the separable model denies it. **The parameter most worth a prior**, and testable against fleet telemetry.
2. **Calibration spread.** A vs B differ by a factor of `r fmt_num(pv_at(params$ref_rate, "B") / pv_at(params$ref_rate, "A"), 1)` in the buyer-level answer at `r fmt_km(params$ref_rate)` km/yr, swamping every financial assumption including the discount rate (section 7.1).
3. **$\pi$ is unobserved.** The lapse results in 6.2 are highly sensitive to per-check compliance, and `r fmt_num(extra_to_toyota, 0)` at-risk checks compound any error geometrically. Real-world $\pi$ for a `r fmt_km(params$increment_km)` km interval is probably well below annual-service compliance rates.
4. **Service margin is a guess.** The `r fmt_dkk(params$service_margin_low)`–`r fmt_dkk(params$service_margin_high)` DKK per visit range drives section 8 entirely. Danish dealer pricing should be checked.
5. **Repair-worthiness is a flat factor.** $\rho = `r params$repair_worthy`$ is applied uniformly, but it should decline with odometer — a `r fmt_km(600000)` km car is less likely to be worth a new pack than a `r fmt_km(250000)` km one. Since the gap probability is concentrated at high odometers, a declining $\rho$ would reduce the PV figures, most in the high-mileage rows where they are largest. Left flat here, but it is a known optimistic bias.
6. **The `r fmt_km(params$subaru_no_grant_km)` km Subaru clause is unmodelled** (section 2). Small, and conservative in direction.
7. **Subaru's Danish terms remain unverified.** Toyota's have now been read directly and confirm every structural assumption (section 1). Subaru's rest on the Norwegian press release, and their Danish *garantibetingelser* and service tariff are both still outstanding — the note is now materially better sourced on one side than the other.
8. **Commercial-use exclusions: confirmed to exist, and narrower than assumed.** Toyota Denmark states *"Særlige regler gælder for Proace og Taxa"* and links to separate commercial pages, which have not been read here. It is easy to read as the item most capable of making the cover worthless for a high-mileage buyer, but that conflates mileage with commercial status. The exclusion names a *van model* and *licensed taxi use*; it is not a distance test. A private owner is outside it at any mileage. It remains load-bearing for the adverse-selection argument in section 7.2, and it is unread, but it is not an item on a private buyer's checklist. The one residual channel is resale: if the marginal second-hand buyer of a very high-mileage EV were a commercial operator, the exclusion would trim the resale premium in section 7.6 — plausible in principle, and small enough not to move the figures here.
9. **Which lapse regime applies is inferred, not stated.** Section 3.3 defaults to reinstatement on the strength of the Relax wording and the battery page's "activate a new guarantee at any time" language. Neither says in terms what happens to the *battery* guarantee after a missed check. Section 6.2 shows both; the choice moves fleet-level lapse effects by an order of magnitude, though it leaves the buyer-level sections untouched.
9. **Realised vs modelled claims.** Payout requires demonstrating sub-`r fmt_pct(params$soh_threshold, 0)` SoH. Measurement disputes, "normal use" clauses and fast-charging abuse exclusions all sit between the modelled crossing probability and a cheque.

---

## 12. Bottom line

- The mechanisms are identical. Only the mileage ceiling differs: `r fmt_km(params$toyota_ceiling_km)` vs `r fmt_km(params$subaru_ceiling_km)` km.
- A mileage cap binds iff it sits below $x_{\text{crit}}$. Toyota's is above; Subaru's is well below.
- Reaching Toyota's ceiling requires `r fmt_num(checks_to_toyota, 0)` dealer visits. The coverage is bought, not given — which is the real reason it is cheap to offer.
- Gross of servicing cost, the difference is worth **nothing below `r fmt_km(gap_opens_at)` km/yr**, `r fmt_dkk(pv_at(params$ref_rate, "A"))`–`r fmt_dkk(pv_at(params$ref_rate, "B"))` DKK at `r fmt_km(params$ref_rate)`, and `r fmt_dkk(pv_at(max(buyer_rates), "A"))`–`r fmt_dkk(pv_at(max(buyer_rates), "B"))` DKK at `r fmt_km(max(buyer_rates))`.
- Net of servicing cost there are **two answers, not one**, and at the buyer's mileage both point the same way. Toyota servicing is dearer than Subaru's by `r fmt_pct(1 - params$service_subaru_small_dkk / params$service_toyota_small_dkk, 1)`–`r fmt_pct(1 - params$service_subaru_large_dkk / params$service_toyota_large_dkk, 1)` per visit, and the Toyota workshop is further away; together those outweigh the gap on both calibrations.
- **You are not choosing for ten years at once.** The base guarantee needs no health check, and cover is reinstatable, so the visits that actually buy the contested cover are the late ones. Returning to a dealer only when Subaru's ceiling falls keeps the whole gap value and cuts the servicing bill sharply (section 7.10).
- **Both franchised service tariffs are quoted**, and the verdict turns on a margin of a few percent between them. That makes it fragile in a checkable way: `r fmt_pct(share_extrap, 0)` of the servicing difference rests on Subaru prices extrapolated beyond the `r fmt_km(params$subaru_quoted_to_km)` km the quote covers, and an uplift of `r fmt_pct(uplift - 1, 1)` on those would reverse it (section 7.4). What remains genuinely missing is an independent quote and the buyer-side cost of a pack. The commercial-use exclusion, flagged in earlier drafts as the top item to verify, is a manufacturer-side defence that does not reach a private owner at any mileage (section 7.2).
- A warranty is a variance-reduction purchase, not an expected-value one. The case for paying up is strongest precisely where the mean cannot be pinned down — and section 1.2 argues the PVs above are lower bounds for a buyer who cannot pool the risk.

**If you are deciding between the two cars**, the order of operations is:

1. **Establish your usage rate honestly.** Below `r fmt_km(gap_opens_at)` km/yr the two contracts are identical and the ceiling is worth exactly nothing — though if the Toyota workshop is further away, choosing it still costs you the extra journeys (section 7.7).
2. **Ask Subaru what a service costs past `r fmt_km(params$subaru_quoted_to_km)` km.** Both tariffs are now quoted, but Subaru's only to `r fmt_km(params$subaru_quoted_to_km)` km — the first five of `r nrow(vis)` visits at your mileage — and the verdict rests on a `r fmt_pct(1 - params$service_subaru_small_dkk / params$service_toyota_small_dkk, 1)` margin holding across the other `r nrow(vis) - sum(vis$km <= params$subaru_quoted_to_km)`. An uplift of `r fmt_pct(uplift - 1, 1)` reverses it. Get one independent quote too, which decides the other scenario; section 7.5 gives the threshold it has to beat.
3. **Ask a dealer for a written out-of-warranty pack replacement price.** The `r fmt_dkk(params$severity_buyer_dkk)` DKK used here is a trade-cost figure standing in for a retail bill, and it makes every buyer-side number an underestimate (section 7.9).
4. **Ask whether you would dealer-service anyway** — and, if so, how far away each workshop is. That answer, plus the distance, decides more than the whole degradation model does.
5. **Put two questions to the dealer about the health check.** Both are cheap to ask and both move real money. *Does a missed check end the battery guarantee, or can a later check reactivate it?* — section 7.10's strategy, worth five figures, depends on the answer being the second. *And is the extension one year or `r fmt_km(params$increment_km)` km, whichever first?* — the battery page says `r fmt_km(params$increment_km)` km, the general warranty page says 12 months, and at your mileage that is the difference between two visits a year and one.
6. **Do not pay much for the ceiling itself.** It costs the manufacturer `r fmt_dkk(decomp$total[1] * params$severity_maker_dkk)`–`r fmt_dkk(decomp$total[2] * params$severity_maker_dkk)` DKK per car to grant. Negotiate on service pricing instead, where the money actually is (section 9).

---

```{r integrity, include=FALSE}
# Post-hoc invariants. These exist because a variable-name collision once left
# `cap_grid` holding capitalisation shares instead of mileage ceilings, which
# silently replaced section 6.1's table with kilometre figures of 0 and 1
# without any error being raised. Anything that would produce nonsense rather
# than a crash belongs here.
stopifnot(
  "cap_grid must still hold mileage ceilings, not shares" =
    all(cap_grid > 1000),
  "cap_table must match the cap grid" =
    identical(sort(cap_table$cap_km), sort(cap_grid)),
  "retained liability must lie in [0, 1]" =
    all(cap_table$retained_a >= 0 & cap_table$retained_a <= 1.0001) &&
    all(cap_table$retained_b >= 0 & cap_table$retained_b <= 1.0001),
  "retained liability must rise with the cap" =
    !is.unsorted(cap_table$retained_a) && !is.unsorted(cap_table$retained_b),
  "fleet truncated must fall as the cap rises" =
    !is.unsorted(rev(cap_table$truncated)),
  "gap must be zero at or below the kink rate" =
    all(buyer_gap$pv_dkk[buyer_gap$rate <= gap_opens_at] == 0),
  "gap PV must rise with usage rate within a calibration" =
    all(buyer_gap |> arrange(calib, rate) |> group_by(calib) |>
          summarise(ok = !is.unsorted(pv_dkk), .groups = "drop") |> pull(ok)),
  "resale split must add back to the full gap" =
    all(abs((holding_tbl$captured_pv + holding_tbl$residual_pv) -
              holding_tbl$gap_full) < 1e-6),
  "capitalised resale cannot exceed the value handed on" =
    all(holding_tbl$resale_pv <= holding_tbl$residual_pv + 1e-9),
  "servicing differential must grow with the usage rate" =
    !is.unsorted(serv |> filter(!dealer_anyway) |> arrange(rate...1) |>
                   pull(pv_dkk)),
  "delaying the dealer must not increase Toyota spend" =
    !is.unsorted(rev(strategy |> filter(calib == "B") |> arrange(sale_year <- dealer_from) |>
                       pull(toy_spend))),
  "severity scaling must be proportional" =
    abs(gap_of(cal$B, my$rate, severity = 2 * params$severity_buyer_dkk)$pv_dkk -
          2 * gap_of(cal$B, my$rate)$pv_dkk) < 1e-6
)
```

## Appendix A — Monte Carlo cross-check

```{r simulation-check, eval=params$use_simulation, cache=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
sim_check <- expand_grid(
  rate = buyer_rates[buyer_rates > gap_opens_at],
  calib = names(cal)
) |>
  mutate(
    analytic = map2_dbl(calib, rate, \(k, r) gap_of(cal[[k]], r)$p_gap),
    mc = map2_dbl(calib, rate, \(k, r) {
      cc <- cal[[k]]
      sim <- simulate_fleet(params$n_sim, cc$a, cc$b, cc$sd_unit, d_crit,
                            params$med_rate, params$sdlog_rate,
                            fixed_rate = r, seed = params$seed)
      ts <- warranty_term(r, params$age_ceiling, params$subaru_ceiling_km)
      tt <- warranty_term(r, params$age_ceiling, params$toyota_ceiling_km)
      mean(sim$t_fail > ts & sim$t_fail <= tt)
    })
  ) |>
  mutate(
    mc_se = sqrt(mc * (1 - mc) / params$n_sim),
    z = (mc - analytic) / mc_se
  )

sim_check |>
  transmute(
    `Annual km` = fmt_km(rate),
    Calibration = calib,
    `Analytic p(gap)` = fmt_pct(analytic, 4),
    `MC p(gap)` = fmt_pct(mc, 4),
    `MC s.e. (pp)` = fmt_num(100 * mc_se, 4),
    `z` = fmt_num(z, 2)
  ) |>
  show_table(caption = paste0("Analytic vs ", fmt_km(params$n_sim),
                              " Monte Carlo draws, seed ", params$seed))
```

```{r simulation-note, results='asis'}
if (!params$use_simulation) {
  cat(
    "*Not run. Set `use_simulation: TRUE` in the YAML header to reproduce the ",
    "analytic results against ", fmt_km(params$n_sim), " Monte Carlo draws. ",
    "The check is disabled by default because the analytic conditional CDF is ",
    "exact, and because at calibration A's gap probabilities (~1e-4) the Monte ",
    "Carlo standard error is a substantial fraction of the estimate — the ",
    "simulation is the noisier of the two, not the reference.*",
    sep = ""
  )
}
```

## Appendix C — Sources

- **Toyota Ireland**, New Car and Battery Warranty — <https://www.toyota.ie/owners/warranty>. EV Battery Guarantee: `r fmt_pct(params$soh_threshold, 0)` minimum capacity to `r params$base_years` years or `r fmt_km(params$base_km)` km. On passing the EV Health Check, EV Battery Extended Care for 1 year or `r fmt_km(params$increment_km)` km, whichever first, up to `r params$age_ceiling` years vehicle age or `r fmt_km(params$toyota_ceiling_km)` km. Mirrored at <https://www.toyotaservice.ie/owners/warranty>.
- **Subaru Norge**, "Subaru lanserer 10 års garanti i Norge", 16 January 2026 — <https://www.mynewsdesk.com/no/subaru-norge/pressreleases/subaru-lanserer-10-aars-garanti-i-norge-3426097>. `r params$age_ceiling` yr / `r fmt_km(params$subaru_ceiling_km)` km service-activated warranty including the high-voltage battery at `r fmt_pct(params$soh_threshold, 0)` minimum capacity, MY2026+, Subaru Norge AS imports; `r fmt_km(params$increment_km)` km per-service increment; no grant past `r fmt_km(params$subaru_no_grant_km)` km.
- Subaru base battery terms of `r params$base_years` yr / `r fmt_km(params$base_km)` km corroborated for Denmark (trade press), Germany (Subaru press release, June 2022), and equivalently 8 yr / 100,000 mi for UK and US.
- Toyota Australia dealer material corroborates the `r params$base_years` yr / `r fmt_km(params$base_km)` km base with `r fmt_pct(params$soh_threshold, 0)` threshold and annual health-check extension for the bZ4X.
- **Toyota Danmark**, battery guarantee — <https://www.toyota.dk/toyotas-drivlinjer/batterigaranti-tryghed>, retrieved 2 September 2026. Two covers: *"Fejl på batteriet"* 5 år / 100.000 km, and capacity at minimum `r fmt_pct(params$soh_threshold, 0)` for `r params$base_years` år / `r fmt_km(params$base_km)` km. Each EV health check adds *"1 år/15.000 km (hvad der kommer først)"* to both, *"helt indtil bilen fylder `r params$age_ceiling` år eller har kørt 1 mio km"*. Checks at an authorised Toyota workshop. *"Særlige regler gælder for Proace og Taxa."*
- **Toyota Danmark**, warranty overview — <https://www.toyota.dk/toyota-ejere/om-toyota-service/derfor-toyota-service/toyota-garanti>, retrieved 2 September 2026. Factory warranty 3 år / 100.000 km. Toyota Relax extends 12 months per authorised service to a maximum of 10 years or 185.000 km. *"Alle standardgarantier overføres til en evt. ny ejer i hele garantiperioden."*
- **Toyota Danmark**, Relax conditions — <https://www.toyota.dk/toyota-ejere/om-toyota-service/derfor-toyota-service/toyota-garanti/relax-betingelser>, retrieved 2 September 2026. Transferable to subsequent owners. A missed or overdue service does not forfeit future cover: *"diskvalificerer dette dig ikke til fremtidig dækning"*, with cover beginning again 30 days after the next completed service. This is the basis for the reinstatable lapse regime in section 3.3, though the wording is Relax's rather than the battery guarantee's.
- **An authorised Subaru workshop in Denmark**, written service quote of 3 September 2026 for an e-Outback Business 5 Door Wagon AWD 280 kW Electric. The workshop is not named and the quote is not reproduced here: it was issued to an individual rather than published as a tariff, and the document itself carries vehicle identifiers. `r fmt_num(params$service_subaru_small_dkk, 2)` DKK incl. VAT at `r fmt_km(params$increment_km)` / 45,000 / 75,000 km (1, 3 and 5 years) and `r fmt_num(params$service_subaru_large_dkk, 2)` DKK at 30,000 / 60,000 km (2 and 4 years) — the same alternating pattern as Toyota. Quoted only to `r fmt_km(params$subaru_quoted_to_km)` km / 5 years.
- **Toyota Køge**, service price calculator — <https://www.toyota-koege.dk/vaerksted/kalkulator>, retrieved 2 September 2026. Lille service `r fmt_dkk(params$service_toyota_small_dkk)` DKK at odd multiples of `r fmt_km(params$increment_km)` km; stort service `r fmt_dkk(params$service_toyota_large_dkk)` DKK at even multiples.
- A Spanish source describes the base high-voltage battery warranty as 5 yr / 100,000 km. That is the defect cover, not the capacity guarantee (section 2.1).
